subject: Mathematics
source: AQA GCSE Mathematics 8300 specification (2015 onwards) — Y11 spec points covering algebra (A7+), ratio and proportion (R), geometry (G), probability (P) and statistics (S). Codes are AQA-standard.

specPoints.specTitle: Where appropriate, interpret simple expressions as functions with inputs and outputs
Work with coordinates in all four quadrants
Plot graphs of equations that correspond to straight-line graphs in the coordinate plane
Identify and interpret gradients and intercepts of linear functions graphically and algebraically
Identify pairs of parallel and perpendicular lines (HT only for perpendicular)

Recognise, sketch and interpret graphs of linear functions, quadratic functions, simple cubic functions, the reciprocal function y = 1/x, exponential functions y = k^x and trigonometric functions (HT for cubic, exp, trig)
Sketch translations and reflections of a given function (HT only)
Plot and interpret graphs in real contexts including distance-time graphs, velocity-time graphs and graphs in financial contexts
Calculate or estimate gradients of graphs and areas under graphs (HT only for non-linear)
Recognise and use equation of a circle with centre at origin (HT only)
Solve linear equations in one unknown algebraically
Solve quadratic equations algebraically by factorising, by completing the square (HT) and by using the quadratic formula (HT)
Solve two simultaneous equations in two variables, including one linear and one quadratic (HT for quadratic)
Find approximate solutions to equations numerically using iteration (HT only)
Translate simple situations or procedures into algebraic expressions or formulae
Solve linear inequalities in one or two variables and represent the solution on a number line, on a graph or in set notation (HT for two variables)
Generate terms of a sequence from a term-to-term or position-to-term rule
Recognise and use sequences of triangular, square and cube numbers, simple arithmetic progressions, Fibonacci-type sequences, quadratic sequences (HT) and geometric progressions
Deduce expressions to calculate the nth term of linear and quadratic sequences (HT for quadratic)
Change freely between related standard units (e.g. time, length, area, volume/capacity, mass)
Use scale factors, scale diagrams and maps
Express one quantity as a fraction of another
Use ratio notation, including reduction to simplest form
Divide a given quantity into two parts in a given part:part or part:whole ratio
Express a multiplicative relationship between two quantities as a ratio or fraction
Understand and use proportion as equality of ratios
Relate ratios to fractions and to linear functions
Define percentage as 'number of parts per hundred'; interpret percentages and percentage changes
Solve problems involving percentage change, including percentage increase and decrease, and original value problems and simple interest
Solve problems involving direct and inverse proportion, including graphical and algebraic representations
Compound units such as speed, rates of pay, unit pricing, density and pressure
Set up, solve and interpret growth and decay problems including compound interest (HT for iterative growth/decay)
Recognise and interpret graphs that illustrate direct and inverse proportion
Interpret the gradient of a straight-line graph as a rate of change
Interpret the gradient at a point on a curve as the instantaneous rate of change (HT only)
Use conventional terms and notations for points, lines, vertices, edges, planes, parallel lines, perpendicular lines, right angles, polygons, regular polygons
Use the standard conventions for labelling and referring to the sides and angles of triangles
Apply the properties of angles at a point, on a straight line, vertically opposite at a point of intersection of two lines
Derive and use the sum of angles in a triangle (e.g. to deduce and use the angle sum in any polygon)
Apply angle facts and triangle congruence to obtain simple proofs (HT for proof)
Apply the concepts of congruence and similarity, including the relationships between lengths, areas and volumes in similar figures

Identify, describe and construct congruent and similar shapes, including on coordinate axes, by considering rotation, reflection, translation and enlargement (including fractional and negative scale factors — HT for negative)
Solve geometrical problems on coordinate axes
Identify and apply circle definitions and properties, including: centre, radius, chord, diameter, circumference, tangent, arc, sector and segment
Apply and prove the standard circle theorems (HT only)
Solve geometrical problems involving the use of Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometric ratios in two dimensions, and Pythagoras and trigonometry in three dimensions (HT for 3D)
Use the sine rule, cosine rule and area = ½ab sin C in any triangle (HT only)
Calculate perimeters and areas of triangles, parallelograms, trapezia, circles and composite shapes; calculate arc lengths, angles and areas of sectors
Calculate surface areas and volumes of cuboids, prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres
Apply the concepts of vectors in geometry, including addition and subtraction of vectors, multiplication of vectors by a scalar, and use vectors in geometric proofs (HT for proofs)
Record, describe and analyse the frequency of outcomes of probability experiments using tables and frequency trees
Apply the property that probabilities of an exhaustive set of outcomes sum to one
Use the basic vocabulary of probability and the 0-1 probability scale
Calculate the probability of independent and dependent combined events using tree diagrams (HT for dependent)
Calculate and interpret conditional probabilities through representation using two-way tables, tree diagrams and Venn diagrams (HT only)
Generate theoretical sample spaces for single and combined experiments and use these to calculate theoretical probabilities
Infer properties of populations or distributions from a sample, while knowing the limitations of sampling

Interpret and construct tables, charts and diagrams, including frequency tables, bar charts, pie charts and pictograms for categorical data; vertical line charts for ungrouped discrete numerical data; tables and line graphs for time-series data
Construct and interpret diagrams for grouped discrete data and continuous data, e.g. histograms with equal and unequal class intervals (HT for unequal) and cumulative frequency graphs

Interpret, analyse and compare distributions of data sets through measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode), spread (range, including consideration of outliers, quartiles and inter-quartile range), and appropriate graphical representations
Apply statistics to describe a population (HT only — sampling and inference)
Use and interpret scatter graphs of bivariate data; recognise correlation; draw and use estimated lines of best fit
